symptom: On mobile, holiday and near-date rails remain on a loader for several seconds and then show a retry error even though valid deals exist; changing tabs can repeat the same sequence.
expected_behavior: A tab press gives immediate local feedback, retains the last verified rail while refreshing, and replaces it with the selected verified data without a blank rail or a false terminal error.
environment: Public https://vii.spaplus.co on 2026-11-12, photographed on iPhone Safari around 12:46-12:47 Israel time; corroborated from the public JSON endpoints and release/v875-holiday-atomic-search-20261111 at 1e5d5884.

steps: Open the public home page or a holiday page on mobile.
Select a holiday or near-date tab whose durable snapshot is cold.
Observe the skeleton and eventual retry state.
Request the same public JSON endpoint repeatedly and compare cache status and timing.
reproduction.evidence: The six user photographs show the loader and retry state. The public Sylvester endpoint first returned availabilityStatus=refreshing with zero deals after 5920ms, then refreshed with 50 deals after 5189ms, then fresh with 50 deals after 1308ms.

observations.observation: The holiday detail client stops one transport attempt at 4000ms while the server is allowed to wait 4800ms before returning refreshing.
The home slider allows 5500ms, but the measured cold public response took 5920ms including origin and edge time.
observations.evidence: app/components/home-live-deals.tsx sliderRequestBudgetMs=5500 and the public endpoint timing captured on 2026-11-12.

observations.observation: A cold holiday cache can return refreshing with no cards, while the next request produces valid results and only a later request is fast.
observations.evidence: Public endpoint sequence: 5920ms refreshing/0, 5189ms refreshed/50, 1308ms fresh/50.

observations.observation: Even verified cache reads still spend material time in display, catalog-index and snapshot reads.
observations.evidence: Public tomorrow response was fresh but took 2458ms; Server-Timing reported roughly 1801-1844ms across display, snapshot and catalog index.

observations.observation: The holiday rail is not server-seeded; it always starts client discovery after activation.
observations.evidence: HomeLiveSections passes initialData only to the near-date HomeLiveDeals instance, not the holidays instance.

hypotheses.mechanism: The client timeout and recovery state machine are shorter than or too close to the server cold-cache path, so valid in-flight work is converted into a false error; incomplete prewarming makes that path user-visible.
hypotheses.prediction: A cold endpoint will exceed the client budget, return refreshing or complete shortly afterward, and a subsequent request will succeed with deals.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Measure the same cold public holiday endpoint three times and compare timings, cache status and deal count to the code budgets.
hypotheses.result: Observed 5920ms refreshing/0, 5189ms refreshed/50 and 1308ms fresh/50 versus client budgets of 4000ms and 5500ms.

hypotheses.mechanism: The screenshots are caused only by stale browser cache on one iPhone.
hypotheses.prediction: Independent no-cache requests would be fast and verified while only the photographed browser failed.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Issue independent no-cache requests to the public API.
hypotheses.result: Independent requests reproduced multi-second refreshing and cold behavior, so device cache is not the cause.

hypotheses.mechanism: The supplier has no deals for the selected holiday.
hypotheses.prediction: Later verified responses would still contain no deals.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Repeat the exact endpoint after the server warm operation finishes.
hypotheses.result: The endpoint returned 50 verified deals, so the error state was false.

fix.change: Not implemented in this diagnostic turn. The causal repair is to make discovery snapshot-first, keep the previous verified rail visible during refresh, treat refreshing as a bounded non-terminal state, align one shared end-to-end deadline, and prove scheduled warming coverage instead of relying on it implicitly.
